A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same teacher-student adapter framework, despite the title change and STICL-to-WILDA renaming. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GLUE/MMLU experiments, ID/OOD comparisons, stability tests, adapter-fusion results, and weak-to-strong generalization analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds hybrid inference, demonstration-reconstruction, and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: The teacher-student training, LoRA adapters, demonstration-selection variants, and adapter summation remain. v2 adds an optional inference variant combining an active adapter with fresh prompt demonstrations (Appendix D.2), extending v1's query-only student inference.

E1.justification: The GLUE tasks, MMLU subsets, and near-OOD dataset transfers remain unchanged. Appendix D.3 adds reconstruction of encoded GLUE demonstrations, introducing a generation/retrieval diagnostic task on existing datasets.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain zero-shot and n-shot ICL, PBFT, ICV, and Batch-ICL. The added hybrid-inference study reuses standard ICL and compares internal WILDA configurations.

E3.justification: v2 adds a comparison allocating 32 labeled examples between adapters and prompts, and a single-demonstration reconstruction protocol using 1,000 examples per GLUE dataset and BERTScore F1. Its GLUE template also omits the demonstration question line present in v1 (Appendices F.1 versus E.1); this documents a prompt revision without establishing that original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices D.2-D.3 add targeted tests of adapter composition with fresh demonstrations and reconstruction of stored demonstrations, including SST/RTE examples. Existing ordering robustness, shot-count, unlabeled-data, adapter-fusion, and weak-to-strong analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4 describes the associations as point-biserial rather than Pearson correlations, retaining -0.968 and -0.916 without establishing recomputation. Original run counts, standard deviations, and significance tests remain. New Table 9 reports 10-run means without deviations, although its reused results retain deviations elsewhere.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1-8 retain their scores and deviations. Table 9 adds the hybrid 16/16 results, including RTE 87.3; Table 10 adds reconstruction BERTScores of 0.80-0.91. Appendix C adds computational-cost estimates, and Table 3 explicitly reports differences between existing ID and OOD scores.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 corrects the Jacobian spectral norm's description from an upper bound to a pointwise lower bound on the global Lipschitz constant, consistent with the retained inequality. Appendix B.2 refines the Frobenius-proxy reasoning; the dual-form derivation and latent-shift decomposition remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central generalization, stability, efficiency, and weak-to-strong claims remain. The abstract and introduction add an explicit claim that learned adapters compose with new inference-time demonstrations; the weak-supervision terminology mainly reframes the existing training approach.

C2.justification: New Appendix C qualifies efficiency through training overhead and approximately 2,100 inferences to amortize it, discusses dependence on unlabeled data, and acknowledges untested scaling to much larger demonstration sets. Appendix D adds interpretations of hybrid inference and reconstruction as evidence about adapter representations.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies full-vocabulary soft teacher targets and penultimate-layer outputs for the Jacobian analysis, and supplies reconstruction prompts and computational-cost information. These are documentation additions; the main LoRA hyperparameters, model specifications, and claimed supplementary-code availability are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cai et al. and Chen et al. on demonstration scaling and the BERTScore reference, while removing the Amini survey, Sonoda-Murata, and Vaswani references. The broader research relationships remain, with emphasis shifted toward weak supervision. Publication updates for retained works do not introduce new comparators.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, experimental setup, and related work undergo extensive rewriting around weak supervision, alongside the title and method renaming. Setup lists become prose, the analysis subsections are merged, and limitations and a conference checklist are added.

P2.justification: v2 adopts NeurIPS formatting and reflows retained displays. It adds Tables 9-10 and reconstruction-example boxes; Table 9 partly redisplays existing results. Table 3 gains ID/OOD differences and a corrected caption, while Figure 2 receives caption and labeling edits without replacing its analyses.

improvement.justification: v2 better qualifies efficiency and applicability through Appendix C, corrects the Lipschitz-bound explanation, and adds focused composability and reconstruction tests. These improve assessment of the retained findings. The gains are limited: reconstruction similarity alone does not establish latent disentanglement, and the GLUE prompt-template revision remains unexplained.
